newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-State Bank NSW to become Colonial State Bank.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-State Bank NSW to become Colonial State Bank.

text.p: Australian insurer The Colonial Group said on Monday it had changed the trading name of the State Bank of New South Wales to Colonial State Bank.
It also said it would launch a chain of new mini-branches at shopping centres in New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland.

"This is a marriage of two strong brands and further strengthens our position as Australia's first financial solutions organisation," Colonial's Group Managing Director Peter Smedley said in a statement.

"It sends a strong message to our customers that they can achieve all their financial solutions through the one outlet," he said. "This includes banking, insurance, funds management, credit cards plus integrated products, which can be adapted to meet the needs of customers at every stage of their life."
Smedley said Colonial was a strong national brand.
Its recognition had increased to 16 percent from two percent in the past three years while the State Bank brand had a strong New South Wales franchise, he said.

"Bringing the two brands together signals the group's intention to extend banking services beyond State Bank's traditional market, and to remind existing customers that they can get more services from the same place," he said.
The bank's headquarters will remain in Sydney.
Colonial Mutual acquired State Bank of New South Wales in 1994. The group plans to list on the Australian Stock Exchange in the first half of calendar 1997.
More combined prodcuts will be launched progressively over the next year, Smedley said.
The Melbourne-based Colonial Group has A$36 billion in funds under management and employs more than 9,800 people in 11 countries.
